title: Countdown Sale Video Maker | AIVideosUGC
description: Make a countdown sale video that says the last day out loud. Paste the product page, pick an avatar, set the end date, and download the file.
lead: Get a sale video that says the last day out loud. Paste the product page, pick an avatar, set the end date, and change the offer line before you download.

faq.q: How many credits do I spend on a sale photo or a sale video?
faq.a: A sale video spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A photo spends 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits, Pro is $35 with 300, and Premium is $63 with 600. You see the cost before you start. If a job fails, those credits come back. A finished file is not refunded just because you dislike it.

faq.q: Can my shop software request a sale video from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. Your tools can request a sale video from a product link through the API. The file stays in your account until you decide to share it.

faq.q: Can one AI avatar present the denim jacket through the sale?
faq.a: Yes. Use the same AI avatar from your other clips, so the sale video looks like the same shop.

faq.q: How do I say the last day in the sale video before I download?
faq.a: Set the end date in the editor before you download, and move it if the sale window shifts. The cream jar stays in frame while you decide when the offer stops.

faq.q: Can I add the clip I already filmed on my table?
faq.a: Paste a product page so the photos come in, upload a picture, or add a clip you already shot. You still check the offer before it goes out.

faq.q: Can I keep the same scene and only swap the next offer?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the product scene and swap the line, the voice, or the end date when the code changes.

faq.q: Can I show the earlier price beside the sale price in the ad?
faq.a: Only if you really charged that earlier price. Check the rules where you sell before an old price sits next to the new one.

faq.q: Can I run the download as a paid sale ad?
faq.a: Yes. The download has no AIVideosUGC watermark, so you can place it as a paid ad. The app you pick still has its own rules.

faq.q: Can I make sale videos for many products in one sitting?
faq.a: Yes. Send several product links and each one comes back as its own ad. Review every file before it is published.

benefits_h2: A Countdown Turns a Sale Into an Event

benefits.t: One AI Avatar for the Sale
benefits.d: One AI avatar carries the denim jacket through this sale, so the hanger clip looks like the same shop as your other videos. Leave open wall space beside the jacket, and that face opens by naming the last day.
benefits.alt: An older man with short gray hair speaks to the camera beside a plain blue denim jacket on a wooden hanger.

benefits.t: A Spoken Pitch With the Deadline
benefits.d: You get a spoken pitch from the picnic blanket page, and the last day lands as the final line. A buyer hears the offer while the hands keep folding the blanket.
benefits.alt: A man with short blonde hair speaks to the camera while folding a checked picnic blanket at a park table.

benefits.t: Slow the Voice on the End Date
benefits.d: A buyer can catch the end date when the voice eases on Thursday night. Pick a warm voice, keep the rest of the line quick, and leave the charging pad in the shot.
benefits.alt: A woman with auburn hair in a bun speaks to the camera, a plain round charging puck on the desk.

benefits.d: Make two cuts of the tea pouch. One opens on the pack beside the mug, and the other opens by naming the last day. Keep the file you want to run.
benefits.alt: A young man with a short buzz cut speaks to the camera beside a blank kraft pouch and a steel travel mug.

reviews.h2: How Sellers Put an End Date on a Sale
reviews.lead: Four sellers use AIVideosUGC to say the last day out loud and post the clip.

items.d: They paste the jacket page and let an avatar say the last day while the denim jacket stays in frame. They post that clip and skip filming the deadline.
They keep the hands folding the checked picnic blanket and put the end date in the spoken line. They use the file in a social post and skip a new shoot when only the date changes.

items.t: Slow the Voice on the Date
items.d: They leave the wireless charging pad in the shot and slow the voice when they say the end date. They run that cut as a paid ad and skip a reshoot for the date.
They make two cuts of the kraft tea pouch beside the mug. One opens on the last day, and they keep the file they want to run. They skip a reshoot when the offer line changes.

trust.h2: How Sellers Ship a Countdown Clip

items.t: Say the Last Day Out Loud
items.d: A denim seller pastes the jacket page, and the opening says the last day while the jacket stays in frame. They redo that opening without booking another film day.
A home seller keeps the picnic blanket scene and draws the new offer from the credit balance they already have. A new code does not start with a new creator invoice.
A small team makes a sale clip for the charging pad and the tea pouch, instead of waiting on one editor for the whole catalog.

items.t: Set the Date, Skip the Shoot
items.d: A skincare seller pastes the cream page and sets the end date in the editor. That stands in for a location day, a talent call, and an edit queue.
A tea seller tries another opening and another voice when the end date moves. They are not stuck with one sale video for the whole month.
One person can brief, generate, and export the weekend set of sale clips after the orders are packed. Nobody else has to stay late for the denim jacket or the tea pouch.
